metadata.title: Hash Table Collisions: Chaining in One Bucket
metadata.subject: Computer Science
metadata.objective: Show keys hashing to buckets and a collision being resolved.
expectedUnderstanding: A fixed table size gives each key one bucket index
Different keys can share a bucket
Chaining resolves a collision without sorting the table

primitives.text: Hash table with 4 buckets: h(k) = k mod 4
Bucket index = k mod 4; an incoming key moves to its bucket.
10 and 22 both hash to b2; an incoming key with h(k)=2 joins their chain.
Collisions are normal. Bucket order is not insertion order or sorted order.

checkpoints.title: One key, one index
checkpoints.body: For this four-bucket table, bucket index = k mod 4. Key 10 hashes to b2 and key 22 also hashes to b2. A fixed table size keeps the same key in the same bucket.

checkpoints.title: A collision is visible
checkpoints.body: Keys 10 and 22 are different, but both land in b2. They are stored together as a chain. Drag the key slider: any incoming key with h(k)=2 joins the same chain.

checkpoints.title: Resolution is not sorting
checkpoints.body: Chaining resolves the collision by keeping multiple entries in b2. The table is not sorted, and bucket order is not insertion order. Move k to 21 and watch the incoming token go to b1 instead.

narration.text: A four-bucket table uses h(k) = k mod 4.
Keys 10 and 22 both land in bucket 2; that is a collision.
Chaining keeps both in b2, while bucket order remains index order.

fallback.text: A hash table with four buckets assigns a key k to bucket k mod 4. Key 10 and key 22 both hash to bucket 2, so they collide. The collision is resolved by chaining: both distinct keys are stored together in bucket 2. The incoming key slider shows a third key moving to its bucket; when its residue is 2 it joins the chain. Chaining does not sort the table, and bucket order does not preserve insertion order. A collision is normal and does not mean the hash function failed.

accessibility.alt: A four-bucket hash table with keys 10 and 22 chained in bucket 2. A slider moves an incoming key token labeled k to bucket k mod 4; when the residue is 2 it joins bucket 2.
